episode_thesis: Brennan argues that trend following works because markets are structural feedback systems: across 68 futures markets since 1984 the Hurst exponent (0.866), fat tails (exponent 3.33) and volatility clustering (0.353) all contradict a memoryless market, and a participant-mix threshold (25-30% divergent) explains regimes. The March 2026 oil spike (66 to 119 to 84) is read as lightning on dry undergrowth, with implications that bell-curve risk and fixed vol targeting understate risk.

worldview_premises.premise: Trend memory sits in magnitude and clustering of moves, not in day-to-day directional autocorrelation, which averages near zero.

worldview_premises.premise: Two participant types: convergent (value, arbitrage, mean reversion) make the narrow peak; divergent (trend, momentum, stop-loss, margin calls) make the fat tails.
worldview_premises.support: Shape of the return distribution plus agent-based simulation

worldview_premises.premise: A market flips regime when divergent participation crosses roughly 25-30%; regimes are observable, not random weather.
worldview_premises.support: Agent-based simulation; link to real markets is argued, not tested

gaps_and_conflicts.issue: Agent-based 25-30% threshold is a simulation result; mapping to real participants is asserted, not shown.
Hurst of 0.866 is much higher than decade averages 0.707-0.757; the estimator and how the 0.866 is computed are not explained.
Autocorrelation 'close to zero' is called a deceptive average, deferred to a later episode.
Oil reading as primed overshoot is one episode and a narrative; positioning data not shown.
Fat-tail frequency (5,791x) depends on the sigma estimate under clustering; not discussed.

forward_looking_inputs: Observable inputs: volatility level, positioning (shorts), momentum, fear, margin levels, supply disruption persistence; horizon months for regime; years for rate cycle. Why: these set the balance of stabilising vs amplifying participants.
reader_inferences: The episode treats unconditional Hurst and tail statistics as proof of trend profitability; these do not by themselves give a tradable edge or its sign.
Both speakers are CTA managers; the conclusions favour their own strategy.

added_claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
added_claims.quote: the efficient market hypothesis, says none of this should exist.
added_claims.claim: Brennan: the independence assumption of the standard model (efficient market hypothesis) implies no persistence, bell-curve returns and steady volatility, so finding all three in every market means the model was wrong from the start; participants watch and respond to each other, creating feedback.
added_claims.testable: partly - conclusion rests on the tests reported in this episode

added_claims.claim: Under bell-curve returns a five-sigma daily move should occur about once in 3.5 million trading days, longer than all liquid-market history; the observed frequency is 5,791 times higher.
